notes: Gathered on 2026-11-20 with WebFetch (page text summarised by a small model); WebSearch used only to find URLs. Several funding pages are roundups that give a week or month, not a day. Investor and company locations are as the pages state; where a page did not state London it is noted. No websummit.com, lu.ma, luma.com, meetup.com or eventbrite pages were fetched. Second pass (2026-11-20): Grow London entry updated from a 11 September 2026 London Stock Exchange page; no current page for the Business Growth Programme could be read.

entries.name: Techstars London Accelerator
entries.what: A three-month, mentorship-driven programme for early-stage founders from anywhere, in all sectors, with help navigating London's capital, talent and markets. The page gives no investment figures.
entries.status: applications open; deadline 2026-11-18 as stated; starts 8 March 2027; Demo Day 3 June 2027

entries.name: Entrepreneurs First (London office)
entries.what: Helps individuals find cofounders and gives early funding. The page lists nine months of office space in central London, an equity-free grant while ideating, up to $250K investment once a company is formed and up to $5M follow-on.

entries.name: Grow London (London & Partners)
entries.what: London & Partners' Grow London programmes. The page, dated 11 September 2026, says Grow London Global supported 265 London scale-up businesses to expand internationally, and that Grow London overall (since 2011) has supported 108,000 additional jobs in London. The page does not say whether the programmes are open to applications.
entries.status: reported active as of 11 September 2026 (page gives results, not application status)

entries.name: London & Partners Business Growth Programme
entries.what: Offered up to £5,000 worth of specialist support and advice, a business growth advisor and workshops in London, for businesses with fewer than 250 employees and turnover below £40m. The page is dated 26 November 2018, so it may be out of date.

entries.name: Gradient Labs Series A (upsized)
entries.what: Upsized Series A of $26M after an initial $13M close. The top-up was led by Octopus Ventures and CommerzVentures, with Redpoint Ventures and Exceptional Capital. The funding is for US growth and product development.

entries.name: Airspeed Series A
entries.what: Series A of $20M (€17.2M) led by DN Capital, with Vi Partners, Framework Venture Partners and Atlassian Ventures. The two weekly roundups give different weeks (1 to 8 and 15 to 22 June 2026).

entries.name: Braid Series A
entries.what: Series A of $38M from Octopus Ventures and KPN Ventures for enterprise connectivity technology. The page lists it among London-based rounds closed in October 2026.

entries.name: Hyperlayer Series A
entries.what: Series A of £19.5M for a programmable banking platform. The page lists it among London-based rounds closed in October 2026.

entries.name: Easol Series A
entries.what: Series A of $20M led by Y Combinator, for a platform for experience businesses with an agentic AI tool for sales, support and operations. Listed among London-based rounds closed in October 2026.

entries.name: Machenta seed round
entries.what: Seed round of $40M from Union Square Ventures and Creandum for a robotics AI model that lets robots learn new tasks from a single demonstration. Listed among London-based rounds closed in October 2026.

entries.name: Gradient Labs
entries.what: London AI startup founded in 2023 by former Monzo engineers. It builds vertical AI agents that automate customer service operations for financial services firms.

entries.name: Airspeed
entries.what: AI go-to-market platform whose agents update CRM records, flag deal risks and draft follow-ups for revenue teams. One roundup says it is London-based with a New York office.

entries.name: Easol
entries.what: Platform for experience businesses, with an agentic AI tool for sales, support and operations.

entries.name: Hyperlayer
entries.what: Programmable banking platform.

entries.name: Braid
entries.what: Enterprise connectivity technology and embedded connectivity infrastructure.

entries.name: Machenta
entries.what: Robotics AI model that lets robots learn new tasks from a single demonstration.

entries.name: Dawn Capital
entries.what: Venture investor focused on B2B for two decades, with a London address on its site. Its site features Flatpay, Runware, Blackwall, Dataiku and Mimecast. No fund sizes stated.

entries.name: Notion Capital
entries.what: Early-stage business software investor with a registered address in London. The page states $2bn assets under management and 200+ companies invested in.

entries.name: Hoxton Ventures
entries.what: Venture firm that invests early in startups. Its footer lists an office at 55 New Oxford Street, London. The page states $369M total capital raised and 90 portfolio companies.

entries.name: LocalGlobe
entries.what: Early-stage fund that backs founders, listed as generalist. The page lists an address at 2 Brill Place, London NW1 1DX. No fund size is stated.

entries.name: Episode 1 Ventures
entries.what: Early-stage investor in B2B software companies raising pre-seed or seed rounds. The footer gives a London office at 112-116 New Oxford Street. The page states £170m total funds raised.

entries.name: Index Ventures
entries.what: Investment firm that backs founders. The footer lists offices in San Francisco, New York and London. No fund size is stated.

entries.name: Connect Ventures
entries.what: Pre-seed and seed investor since 2012, backing technical founders in AI, hardware and automation. The page says it invests across Europe from its home in London and leads or co-leads rounds of $500k to $5m.

entries.name: firstminute capital
entries.what: Early-stage fund investing in European founders across AI and deep tech. The footer gives an address at 180 Strand, London. The page states £1m to £3m tickets and $500m AUM.

entries.name: King's Start-up Accelerator (King's College London)
entries.what: Six-month programme of workshops and sprints plus three months of follow-on support, open to King's students and alumni. It lists grant funding worth £65K in total and office space in Bush House. Ventures pledge 3% of shares if they reach stated success criteria within five years.
entries.status: applications for the 2026-27 cohort closed; next window not stated

entries.name: London Business School Incubator Programme
entries.what: Incubator for LBS alumni start-up founders, run by the Institute of Entrepreneurship and Private Capital. It lists mentorship, workshops, office hours and bursaries. No fee is stated.
entries.status: 2026 applications closed 28 April 2026; wildcard entry before 1 September as stated

entries.name: Roehampton Startup Incubator & Accelerator
entries.what: Free programme for University of Roehampton graduates with a business idea or early-stage venture, with workshops, coaching, mentors and demo days. The page says it is in London.
entries.status: next cohort late August to October 2026 as stated; page said open for applications

entries.name: Capsa AI Series A
entries.what: Series A of $18m, co-led by TX Ventures and Pivot Investment Partners, with Bek Ventures. The article calls Capsa AI a London and New York-based startup building an AI operating system for private capital.
